methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study of 159 patients with appropriate histopathological confirmation. Stratified 5-fold cross-validation implemented with appropriate hyperparameter tuning within folds. However, feature selection performed prior to cross-validation, introducing optimistic bias in performance estimates. Authors acknowledge class imbalance (LRH-EC 108 vs HRH-EC 51) affecting sensitivity. No external validation cohort. FDR correction and correlation-based redundancy reduction appropriate but result in loss of information.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective imaging study addressing clinically relevant question of preoperative risk stratification in endometrial cancer. Moderate discriminative performance (AUC 0.709 with ANN) demonstrates utility but not sufficient for independent clinical decision-making. Authors appropriately acknowledge need for external validation before clinical implementation. PET/CT imaging is standard modality supporting clinical relevance.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods comprehensively described with TRIPOD elements partially addressed (cohort definition, image protocol, feature extraction using IBSI-compliant LIFEx software detailed). Limitations section thorough and candid. However, no statement of data or code availability; raw imaging data and trained models not mentioned as accessible. Reproducibility across different radiomics platforms not addressed. Segmentation threshold justification limited.

novelty_literature.justification: Application of [18F]-FDG PET/CT radiomics to endometrial cancer risk stratification is incremental rather than novel. Multiple prior studies of MRI-based radiomics in EC cited (Refs 20-21). Study demonstrates moderate performance but limited mechanistic novelty or biological insights beyond confirming metabolic heterogeneity correlates with histological grade.

writing_presentation.justification: Methodologically sound presentation with comprehensive methods and results sections. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within literature and acknowledges limitations. However, extensive discussion of moderate performance findings (AUC 0.709) with minimal differences between algorithms makes manuscript somewhat verbose. Figures effectively communicate model performance. Accessible to radiomics-focused audience.

key_strengths: Appropriate use of FDR-controlled feature selection and Pearson correlation filtering to reduce dimensionality from 123 to 16 features
Comprehensive comparison of six machine learning algorithms with multiple statistical tests (DeLong, McNemar) for model comparison
Rigorous PET/CT imaging protocol with standardized acquisition and IBSI-compliant radiomic extraction
Honest reporting of limitations including class imbalance, lack of molecular classification, and absence of external validation
key_concerns: Modest discriminative performance (AUC 0.709) insufficient for independent clinical decision-making without external validation
Feature selection performed before cross-validation introduces optimistic bias in performance estimates; internal CV only
No external validation cohort; single-center retrospective design limits generalizability
Class imbalance (68% LRH-EC vs 32% HRH-EC) and absence of molecular subtyping (FIGO 2023) limits clinical applicability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically rigorous but internally validated only. Moderate performance and lack of external validation limit clinical translation. Appropriate for Tier 3 with major revisions requiring: (1) external multicenter validation; (2) larger sample size with balanced class distribution; (3) integration of molecular subtyping per FIGO 2023.
